title: Jacket Potato with Tuna Mayonnaise
subtitle: Baked potato with a creamy tuna filling
excerpt: A proper baked potato with a crisp skin and fluffy interior, topped with a well-seasoned tuna and spring onion mayonnaise. The classic British lunch, done without shortcuts.

recipe.sourceNotes: The jacket potato, or baked potato, has been a staple of British cooking since the nineteenth century. Tuna mayonnaise became one of the most popular fillings in British workplace cafeterias and lunch counters from the 1970s onwards, alongside baked beans and cheese. The combination became shorthand for everyday British lunch food. Getting the skin crisp requires a hot oven and dry potato, not the wrapping in foil that some recipes recommend, which steams rather than bakes the skin.

content.text: The keys to a good jacket potato: a large, floury potato (Maris Piper or King Edward), a dry surface, and a hot oven. Rub the skin with oil and salt and bake directly on the oven rack for a truly crisp skin. Do not wrap in foil. An 80-minute bake at 200 C gives a skin that crackles and a fluffy interior. The tuna filling needs generous seasoning and something sharp, a squeeze of lemon or a small spoon of capers.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Dry the potatoes well. Rub each all over with olive oil and salt. Prick all over with a fork. Place directly on the oven rack and bake for 75 to 80 minutes until the skin is crisp and the potato gives when squeezed.
Mix the tuna, mayonnaise, spring onions, and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut a deep cross in the top of each potato. Squeeze from the base to open it. Add a knob of butter inside if you like. Top generously with the tuna mayonnaise and serve immediately.
